coverage_limits: OpenAlex was unavailable for the whole run (anonymous daily budget exhausted, HTTP 429), so no OpenAlex keyword searches or citing-work passes on key lane papers were done, and Semantic Scholar also returned 429; citation chasing was therefore not done. The arXiv API rate-limited intermittently, so some records were confirmed from arXiv abstract pages instead. Several publisher pages (SSRN, ScienceDirect, ACM DL) were blocked, so five records (Xiao et al. SSRN; Shaer et al. SSRN; Liu et al. TSC; Luan et al. and Steppe et al. AoM) carry only Crossref title and author data and their designs are unconfirmed, and sample sizes are null when abstracts did not state them. The eight-consecutive-empty-queries stopping rule was not reached: the last rounds still added one to three borderline HCI system studies per four queries, so full CHI 2026, C&C 2026, DIS 2026 and UIST 2026 programs, non-English journals, and education journals remain only partly covered. One WebFetch summary (ICCC 2026 'Before the Prompt') was found to be fabricated on PDF check and was dropped; other design details taken from summaries are flagged in evidence.

candidates.title: Creative Momentum Transfer: How Timing and Labeling of AI Suggestions Shape Iterative Human Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2025)
candidates.task: two-round ideation on plastic pollution solutions
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects experiment crossing timing of AI suggestions (at the outset vs mid-process) with labeling (AI-labeled vs unlabeled), with a no-AI control; outcomes were rated creativity, anchoring and adoption of AI ideas. Crossref also holds a record 10.24963/ijcai.2024/1142 with the same title, apparently a duplicate registration.

candidates.title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
candidates.task: marketing campaign for a fictional startup
candidates.evidence: Participants were randomized to a generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized LLM assistant (no no-AI arm); campaigns from personalized-AI users were rated higher in quality and creativity.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human Machine Creative Problem-Solving
candidates.authors: Rosenbaum, David, Kaufman, Ravid, Ronen, Krebs
candidates.task: ideas to make libraries attractive to young adults
candidates.evidence: Undergraduates were randomized to a coach-like LLM with divergent and convergent personas or to a standard ChatGPT control (no no-AI arm); originality was scored by embedding-based semantic distance (101 analyzed of 105 recruited).

candidates.title: Designing Human and Generative AI Collaboration
candidates.task: 1,000-word short story writing in a classroom
candidates.evidence: Students wrote a story without AI on day 1, then were randomly assigned to one of three ChatGPT collaboration designs (Human Confirmation, Human Creativity, Copilot); outcomes were story quality and interestingness and genre and story similarity across participants, which rose when humans were excluded from ideation. The no-AI baseline is the within-person day-1 story.

candidates.title: Human Thinking under Plural LLM Assistance: Mathematical Problem Solving and Open-Ended Writing
candidates.task: argumentative and creative essay writing (plus a separate math experiment)
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects conditions with no LLM, a single generalist assistant, or a pair of role-specialized assistants; essay quality was rubric-rated and idea diversity computed from embedded key points, and the specialized pair preserved more diversity than the single assistant. 562 participants across two experiments, 247 usable in the writing study.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered 2x2 RCT crossing access to an AI writing assistant (AI vs self) with incentives (originality relative to peers vs quality); collective diversity was measured with embedding and n-gram similarity, and originality incentives raised diversity among AI users. Quality was not measured.

candidates.title: Framing an AI with Values Reduces AI Reliance in AI-supported Writing Tasks
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT 2026)
candidates.task: AI-supported essay writing by Indian and American participants
candidates.evidence: All participants wrote with AI autocomplete suggestions under no intervention, an overview of the AI's framed values, or the values compared with their own; outcomes were AI reliance and textual uniqueness (type-token ratio and cosine similarity across essays). Assignment not described as random; no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
candidates.evidence: Design students were randomly assigned to self-reflection (no AI), stepwise written guidance (no AI), or an antagonistic AI agent that enacts stakeholder conflict; outcomes were counts of ideas generated, edited and discarded and self-rated reconsideration, not rated creativity.

candidates.title: Scanvas: Discovering and Developing Synergistic Opportunities in Generative Design Spaces
candidates.evidence: User study with professional designers comparing the Scanvas system with LLM ideation baselines (no no-AI arm); participants surfaced higher-quality, synergistic concepts.

candidates.title: NexusAI: Enabling Design Space Exploration of Ideas through Cognitive Abstraction and Functional Decomposition
candidates.task: design ideation with decomposed LLM inspiration
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study comparing a diagramming system that decomposes and recombines LLM-generated inspiration with a baseline; outcomes were design-space exploration, fixation and reframing. No no-AI arm.

candidates.title: FlexMind: Supporting Deeper Creative Thinking with LLMs
candidates.authors: Yang, Mohanty, Chen, Hong, Martelaro, Kittur
candidates.evidence: Study comparing ideation with the FlexMind scaffold against ChatGPT; participants generated higher-quality ideas with FlexMind. Sample size not stated in the abstract; no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: IdeaSynth: Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Lab study comparing IdeaSynth (facet canvas with literature-grounded LLM feedback) with a strong LLM baseline; participants explored more alternative ideas and elaborated ideas further. Outcome is exploration and detail rather than rated creativity; no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: PersonaFlow: Designing LLM-Simulated Expert Perspectives for Enhanced Research Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference (DIS 2025)
candidates.evidence: User studies of a system that simulates multiple domain-expert personas with LLMs, compared with alternative designs; outcomes include perceived relevance and creativity of research directions (self-reported) and critical-thinking activity.

candidates.title: CreativeConnect: Supporting Reference Recombination for Graphic Design Ideation with Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2024)
candidates.task: graphic design ideation from reference images
candidates.evidence: User study comparing CreativeConnect with a baseline system without the generative pipelines; participants produced more design ideas and reported higher creativity (self-reported).

candidates.title: Rapid AIdeation: Generating Ideas With the Self and in Collaboration With Large Language Models
candidates.task: rapid ideation workshop on practical issues
candidates.evidence: Workshop in which participants brainstormed on their own and with an LLM; LLM-assisted ideas showed greater variety but not necessarily higher quality than self-generated ideas. Within-person comparison; collaboration styles were also coded.

candidates.title: When and How AI Should Assist Brainstorming for AI Impact Assessment
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT 2026)
candidates.task: team brainstorming for AI impact assessment
candidates.evidence: Ten in-person workshops evaluated co-designed AI interventions for team brainstorming; AI improved rated impact-assessment quality for one use case but not for another, and the authors derive guidance on when AI should hint versus propose. Comparison conditions and assignment are not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Exploring the Impact of AI Value Alignment in Collaborative Ideation: Effects on Perception, Ownership, and Output
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA 2024)
candidates.task: brainstorming practical solutions with an AI agent
candidates.evidence: Participants brainstormed with AI agents holding different values; ideas reflected the agent's values while self-rated idea quality did not differ. No creativity rating or diversity metric is reported in the abstract, so relevance is uncertain.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects comparison of a GenAI-assisted storytelling system with a traditional storyboard (no AI); rated creativity and richness improved and the quality gap between children narrowed (convergence of quality, not of content).

candidates.title: Dynamics of collective creativity in AI art competitions
candidates.evidence: Analysis of 130,882 images from 368 Artbreeder remix parties over 13 months; images grow simpler and converge toward common thematic attractors, and novelty of parent images predicts novelty of children. Context study; no assignment of AI.

candidates.title: Creo: From One-Shot Image Generation to Progressive, Co-Creative Ideation
candidates.authors: De Simone, Boggust, Durand, Wilson, Satyanarayan
candidates.task: designing living room and kitchen images
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects counterbalanced comparison of a multi-stage sketch-to-image system with a one-shot prompt baseline (ChatGPT); homogeneity was measured by CLIP distance between first and final images in each session (a within-session measure), and Creo outputs were less homogeneous. No no-AI arm.

candidates.title: IdeaBlocks: Expressing and Reusing Divergent Intents for Graphic Design Exploration using Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Designing Interactive Systems Conference (DIS 2026)
candidates.task: graphic design exploration with image generation
candidates.evidence: Comparative study of a tool for expressing and reusing divergent intents versus a baseline generative tool; participants explored 2.13 times more images with 12.5% greater visual diversity. No no-AI arm.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Recursive Divergence and Convergence in Story Ideation
candidates.authors: Kim, Kay, Sun, Roemmele, Kreminski, Chung
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study comparing Reverger, which scaffolds recursive divergence and convergence, with a comparable baseline; users explored more unexpected and diverse high-level directions. Sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Expandora: Broadening Design Exploration with Text-to-Image Model
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA 2025)
candidates.task: visual design reference exploration with text-to-image
candidates.evidence: User study comparing Expandora (LLM-generated prompt variations at chosen diversity levels) with a baseline; it increased prompt diversity and the number of prompts tried. Outcome is exploration diversity rather than rated creativity.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.task: idea generation by independent humans versus LLM samples
candidates.evidence: Four studies compare the diversity of ideas from independent human samples and LLM samples and test prompting fixes; ordinary personas improved LLM pool diversity and chain-of-thought reduced fixation in LLMs but not in humans. Context: no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing HAICo (switchable divergent and convergent modes with associative-thinking prompting) with ChatGPT; HAICo outperformed ChatGPT on several creativity dimensions. No no-AI arm.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.authors: Lin, Kang, Martelaro, Kittur, Chen, Hong
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: product design concept exploration with text-to-image
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing a sketch-driven analogical text-to-image tool with ControlNet; Inkspire gave more inspiration and exploration of design ideas. Sample size not in abstract; no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: I Can Embrace and Avoid Vagueness Myself: Supporting the Design Process by Balancing Vagueness through Text-to-Image Generative AI
candidates.evidence: User study with fashion designers comparing CLAY, which balances prompt vagueness, with their existing practice; reported shorter design time and expanded creative possibilities, largely self-reported.

candidates.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
candidates.task: essay writing over four sessions with EEG
candidates.evidence: Participants were divided into LLM, search-engine and brain-only groups for three sessions; in session 4 (n=18) LLM users wrote without tools and brain-only users used the LLM. Essays were scored by teachers and an AI judge and showed within-group homogeneity in named entities, n-grams and topics. Assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI’s Impact on Creative Tasks
other_versions: arXiv 2412.03963 (Augmenting Minds or Automating Skills: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI's Impact on Creative Tasks)
candidates.task: flash fiction writing and song composition
candidates.evidence: Two randomized controlled experiments compare creative work with and without generative AI and test how general versus domain-specific human capital moderates AI's effect on the creative output. The AoM record is an abstract; the arXiv version is the full paper.

candidates.title: Reflexa: Uncovering How LLM-Supported Reflection Scaffolding Reshapes Creativity in Creative Coding
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study of an LLM reflection scaffold for creative coding; structured reflection patterns were linked to broader exploration and higher originality and aesthetic quality. The comparison condition is not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: CommSketch: How Speaking while Sketching Steers Human--AI Design Ideation
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects study comparing an AI design interface that interprets sketches plus concurrent speech with sketch-only input; outcomes are mainly perceived alignment and creativity support rather than rated creativity.

candidates.title: Central Tendency Bias in Human Selection of AI-Generated Design Variations
candidates.venue: IEEE HAXD 2026 (2nd International Conference on Human-AI Interaction and Experience) proceedings
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment manipulating the variance of AI-generated design sets (high vs low) and recording which designs people select; higher variance raised selection of center-proximal designs, constraining selection diversity. No no-AI arm.

candidates.title: Towards Cognitive Process-Aware Proactive Writing Support
candidates.task: creative writing with proactive AI suggestions
candidates.evidence: Two within-subjects studies of a proactive writing assistant that infers writers' cognitive processes to select the type of support; reports better expressiveness and idea exploration than comparison conditions (details not in the abstract).

candidates.title: TreeWriter: AI-Assisted Hierarchical Planning and Writing for Long-Form Documents
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study comparing a hierarchical AI writing editor with Google Docs plus Gemini; TreeWriter improved idea exploration and development and perceived control (self-reported).

candidates.title: Do Conversational Interfaces Limit Creativity? Exploring Visual Graph Systems for Creative Writing
candidates.task: creative writing with chained generative models
candidates.evidence: Small user study comparing a node-based visual graph system for chaining generative models with a similar conversational interface; the graph system supported ideation for some users. Creativity is not formally scored in the abstract.

candidates.title: Varif.ai to Vary and Verify User-Driven Diversity in Scalable Image Generation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference (DIS 2025)
candidates.task: generating diverse image sets for ideation
candidates.evidence: Controlled evaluation comparing Varif.ai (LLM-driven verification and variation of user-specified attributes) with baseline methods; users reached diverse image sets more effectively. Outcome is the diversity of user-steered AI image sets.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment comparing a text-and-image AI-assisted workflow with human-only brainstorming; experts rated AI outputs higher on problem framing but human-only outputs higher on innovation and solution strategies.

candidates.title: Help That Hurts: The Creativity Cost of Generative AI Ideation in Music Composition
candidates.evidence: RCT assigning musically trained individuals to an AI-ideation group (text-to-music) or a no-AI control; external evaluators rated melodies from the AI group as less creative, partly through changed stylistic choices.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment.
candidates.task: employee creativity at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment randomly assigning employees to receive LLM assistance or not; supervisor and external evaluator ratings of creativity rose with LLM assistance, especially for employees high in metacognitive strategies.

candidates.title: The Effect of AI Integration on Designers' Creativity in the Sketching Process for Design Ideation
candidates.venue: Korea Institute of Design Research Society 9(4): 75-86
candidates.evidence: Experiment comparing designers who used AI tools (ChatGPT 4.0 and DALL-E) with designers using traditional sketching; independent-samples t-tests on creativity scores favored the AI group. Assignment and N not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Symbiotic Ceiling in Generative-AI-Assisted Design: Measuring Creativity, Human Agency, and Cultural Specificity in Human-AI Interaction
candidates.evidence: Mixed-method experiment with novice designers across four AI-support conditions; unstructured AI use gave more polish but lower expert-rated originality, cultural specificity and visual diversity than scaffolded AI use. The Crossref title shows a stray comma after the colon.

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of AI features on collaborative creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Australasian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI 2024), pp. 480-489
candidates.task: pair ideation in a digital collaboration tool
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with participants in pairs comparing a collaboration tool with versus without AI features for divergent thinking, sense-making and convergence; AI-supported pairs produced more novel but less appropriate ideas.

candidates.title: DesignAID: Using Generative AI and Semantic Diversity for Design Inspiration
candidates.venue: Proceedings of The ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI 2023), pp. 1-11
candidates.task: creating mood boards with LLM-expanded image generation
candidates.evidence: Crowdsourced designers used a low-diversity Direct Input mode and a high-diversity LLM New Idea mode in a factorial design, compared against Pinterest image search; outcomes were designers' ratings of inspiration, enjoyment and usefulness. A MIT Sloan summary reports 87 designers; Rick et al. (2025) analyze 111 of 115 users.

candidates.title: How far afield should you go when being creative? Semantic area as a metric of AI's effects on creative ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Computational Creativity (ICCC 2025)
candidates.task: mood-board ideation (reanalysis of the DesignAID experiment)
candidates.evidence: Reanalysis of the DesignAID experiment (Direct vs Diverse LLM idea modes) with a semantic-area metric; people who saw a more diverse set of AI ideas selected more diverse ideas, but objective evaluators rated their selections less innovative.

candidates.title: When AI Says No: Investigating the Creative Power of Dissent
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Computational Creativity (ICCC 2025), short paper
candidates.evidence: Compares co-creative storytelling with a dissenting versus a conforming AI; participants produced more creative output with the dissenting AI, though differences were not statistically significant. Details from the ICCC 2025 program listing only.

candidates.title: Playing Along: Building AI Agents for Co-Creation of Improvised Stories
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Computational Creativity (ICCC 2025)
candidates.evidence: Compares stories that people co-created with an LLM agent versus with a human partner in the 'Yes! and...' improv game; rated novelty, value and surprise did not differ. Details from the ICCC 2025 program listing only.

candidates.title: Supermind Ideator: How scaffolding Human-AI collaboration can increase creativity
other_versions: arXiv 2311.01937 (earlier system description with a different title)
candidates.evidence: Experimental study comparing people using the scaffolded Supermind Ideator, people using ChatGPT, and people working alone; Supermind users produced significantly more innovative ideas.

candidates.title: When AI Joins the Brainstorm: Impacts of Generative Language Models on Collaborative Divergent Thinking
candidates.venue: ICIS 2025 Proceedings (46th International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.evidence: Randomized 2x2 experiment varying idea-sharing structure (live vs round-based) and the presence of a generative-language-model AI peer; the AI's ideas were more original, but exposure to them lowered participants' fluency and originality.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Ideation and the performance of Innovation Teams (Preprint)
candidates.task: team idea generation in the innovation process
candidates.evidence: Framed field experiment comparing teams using a custom AI-augmented ideation tool with control teams; AI-augmented teams produced higher-quality ideas in less time with greater idea diversity. Assignment details not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Enhancing designer creativity through human–AI co-ideation: a co-creation framework for design ideation with custom GPT
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e22
candidates.evidence: Design case study comparing co-ideation with a custom GPT that guides context-mapping questions against ideation without AI; novelty and quality were higher with the custom GPT while variety did not differ. N=48 from the article page.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C 2026)
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI image tool
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study comparing text, sketch, and sketch-plus-tags input to an AI creativity support tool; sketch input tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in variety, originality and quality.

candidates.title: Multi-agent AI systems outperform human teams in creativity
candidates.evidence: Compares 4,541 ideas from multi-agent LLM teams with 341 ideas from human teams; LLM teams scored higher in rated creativity, driven by novelty. Context: no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: AI-AI co-creation outperforms human pairs in creative tasks
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-AI co-creation (complementary or identical roles), single-AI creation and human pairs; trained judges rated 1,212 ideas and both AI-AI conditions beat human pairs on creativity and novelty. Context: no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit Human-AI Collaboration: How Supportive and Contrarian AI Personas Reshape Interaction
candidates.task: creative movie-plot task in online triads
candidates.evidence: Students were randomly assigned to 97 triads that were human-only or included an undisclosed supportive or contrarian AI persona; contrarian AI produced more challenge-rich discourse but no gain in creative performance and lower satisfaction.

candidates.title: The Social Blindspot in Human-AI Collaboration: How Undetected AI Personas Reshape Team Dynamics
candidates.task: analytical, creative and ethical tasks in triads
candidates.evidence: Mixed-design experiment with fully human triads or hybrid triads containing an undisclosed supportive or contrarian AI teammate; the abstract reports psychological safety and discussion quality, not creativity of output, so relevance is uncertain.

candidates.title: NarrativeLoom: Enhancing Creative Storytelling through Multi-Persona Collaborative Improvisation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: story writing with multiple AI personas
candidates.evidence: Controlled study comparing stories co-authored with a multi-persona AI system against a comparison condition; experts rated NarrativeLoom stories higher on Torrance fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration.

candidates.title: Proactive AI as a Catalyst for Creativity? Balancing Human Agency and AI Contribution in Collaborative Story Writing
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Wizard-of-Oz within-subjects study (a human wizard acts as the AI) comparing intrusive next-sentence suggestions with non-intrusive exploratory proposals; proactive suggestions raised creativity and speed but traded off perceived agency. Assistance came from a simulated AI.

candidates.title: ChatGPT Destekli Dönütlerin İlkokul Öğrencilerinin Yaratıcı Yazma Becerilerine Etkisi
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest quasi-experiment: one class received ChatGPT-supported feedback with teacher-guided rewriting for six weeks, the control class wrote without feedback; creative writing product scores improved in the experimental class. Title translates as 'The Effect of ChatGPT-Supported Feedback on Primary School Students' Creative Writing Skills'.

candidates.title: How Ai Content Strategies and Participation Styles Affect Team Emergent States and Creativity in Ideation
candidates.task: team ideation with AI content strategies
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how AI content strategies and participation styles affect team emergent states and ideation creativity; the abstract could not be retrieved (SSRN blocked, Crossref has none), so design and outcomes are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Human–AI synergy: finding cognitive balance in idea generation for product innovation
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with three conditions (no AI, moderate AI assistance, high AI assistance); moderate assistance produced the most original and feasible ideas, while high assistance reduced originality and raised overconfidence.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI model type and visual stimuli type on design creativity
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e17
candidates.evidence: 2x2 between-groups experiment crossing AI model type (text-to-image ChatGPT-4o vs image-to-image Midjourney) with figurative vs abstract visual stimuli; text-to-image tools and abstract stimuli raised rated design creativity. No no-AI arm; groups balanced by year, random assignment not stated.

candidates.title: GenAI and Search Tools in Design Education: Comparative Analysis of Student Creativity, Outcomes, and Experiences
candidates.venue: AHFE International, Human Factors in Training, Education, and Learning Sciences, Vol. 231
candidates.evidence: Three conditions (no tool, Pinterest image search, Midjourney image generation); experts rated outputs on originality, effectiveness, usability and feasibility, and generative AI raised originality while search raised feasibility but risked homogenization. Author order follows the PDF; Crossref lists Xia, Jin, Qi.

candidates.title: Augmented (or Not): The Human–GenAI Tango in Generating Creative Ideas
candidates.evidence: Experiment varying how GPT-4 is integrated into ideation; simple integration gave no improvement, while seeding with GPT-4 ideas generated under transformational-creativity principles raised novelty and utility but lowered feasibility. Design details from the City Research Online record.

candidates.title: Future AI Systems: Human–AI Collaborative Teams Outperform Human-Only Teams in Design Ideation
candidates.evidence: Human-subject study comparing two-human teams with human-plus-AI teams in which an AI 'Disruptive Interjector' offers suggestions; trained judges rated ideas from human-AI teams higher. Whether the AI is generative is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Facilitating Asynchronous Idea Generation and Selection with Chatbots
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Australasian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI 2024), pp. 305-323
candidates.evidence: Participants generated and selected ideas with one of two facilitator chatbots (structured vs adaptive process); both helped users build on others' ideas. Whether idea creativity was scored is unclear from the abstract; no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Brainwriting: Investigating the use of LLMs in group ideation
candidates.authors: Shaer, Cooper, Mokryn, Kun, Ben Shoshan
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2024)
candidates.evidence: Evaluates a group-AI brainwriting framework in which an LLM joins group ideation, analyzing the ideation process and the resulting solution space, and compares LLM idea evaluation with expert and novice ratings.

candidates.title: Co-Ideation Across Dimensions: The Effects of Mediation Mode on Creative Collaboration and Ai Co-Ideation
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how mediation mode affects creative collaboration and AI co-ideation; the abstract could not be retrieved (SSRN 403, Crossref has none), so design and outcomes are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Exploring the Potential for Generative AI-based Conversational Cues for Real-Time Collaborative Ideation
candidates.task: remote triad brainstorming with real-time cues
candidates.evidence: Wizard-of-Oz probe in which human facilitators played an AI agent sending contextual cues to 14 brainstorming triads, to derive principles for generative-AI conversational support; no real generative AI. Precursor to the collected Rayan (2025) study.

candidates.title: The Dynamics of Collective Creativity in Human-AI Hybrid Societies
other_versions: arXiv 2502.17962v1 titled 'The Dynamics of Collective Creativity in Human-AI Social Networks'
candidates.evidence: Large online experiment in which networks of humans, AI agents, or both iteratively modified stories; AI-only networks were initially more creative and diverse, but hybrid networks became more diverse than AI-only networks over time. N=879 from a v1 HTML snippet.

candidates.title: Human-AI Synergy Supports Collective Creative Search
candidates.evidence: Compares human-only (social and asocial), AI-only (Gemini agents) and hybrid human-AI groups in a creative search task; hybrid groups performed best while preserving high diversity of guesses. Group sizes (50, 46, 28 humans) from a search snippet; the task is only partly a creative-production task.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.venue: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Working Paper No. 16/2026
candidates.task: open-ended creative writing in the lab
candidates.evidence: Lab experiment randomly assigning participants to ChatGPT access or not, crossed with incentive schemes; Prolific evaluators scored creativity, and gains came only from active AI use, with a concave relation to the number of queries.

candidates.title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence (AI): Field and experimental evidence on the Goldilocks (curvilinear) effect of human–AI collaboration.
candidates.evidence: Experiments with 139 business professionals and 319 working adults who collaborated with ChatGPT at varying intensity, plus a 188-person field survey; moderate collaboration produced the highest rated creative performance, via generating diverse ideas. Design details from the Prolific citations page.

candidates.title: Influence of AI Use on Creativity in a Speculative Design Process
candidates.venue: ASME IDETC-CIE 2025, Volume 4 (22nd International Conference on Design Education; 37th DTM), V004T06A011
candidates.evidence: Experts rated 120 ideas generated by humans alone, by humans using AI as a tool, or by AI alone; AI-involved ideas were rated more well-crafted with no novelty difference, and AI-generated ideas covered a smaller design space. Distinct from the collected Koolman (2026) paper.

candidates.title: AI-generated inspiration for the design process: effects across the vividness of visual imagery spectrum
candidates.venue: International Journal of Design Creativity and Innovation 14(3): 171-189
candidates.evidence: Half of the participants saw AI-generated images for inspiration and half started from scratch; AI inspiration did not improve design quality or speed overall but removed the performance gap between people with low and high visual imagery. Design details from a secondary summary; Crossref has no abstract.

candidates.title: Exploring ChatGPT's impact on student-team ideation outcomes for new product development: a pilot study
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (E&PDE 2024), pp. 533-538
candidates.task: student-team ideation for new product development
candidates.evidence: Pilot with two parallel workshops, one using ChatGPT-assisted ideation and one analogue; fluency and flexibility were slightly lower and the analogue group produced about twice as many original ideas.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing with robot–LLM integration: The interplay of embodiment, AI creativity and user engagement
candidates.evidence: Five conditions: human-human, or human-computer or human-robot with a high- or low-creativity LLM; expert and computational ratings of originality, imagery, voice and flow showed robot embodiment amplifying originality with the high-creativity LLM, while human pairs led on style.

candidates.title: How AI Processing Delays Foster Creativity: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2024)
other_versions: arXiv 2310.06155 (CoQuest: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent)
candidates.task: research question co-creation with an LLM agent
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study comparing breadth-first and depth-first generation (different degrees of AI initiative); higher AI initiative yielded outcomes rated more creative (novelty, surprise) at a cost to experience, and AI processing delays led to more questions.

candidates.title: FIERO: Empowering Creative Writing Through Collaborative Game Play
candidates.task: collaborative storytelling card game with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Compares a multiplayer card game whose interface uses generative AI to synthesize contributions and generate visuals with online collaborative writing alone; the game raised idea fluency, novelty and plot coherence. The AI effect is bundled with the game format.

candidates.title: GraphStory: Collaborative Story Writing through Event-Based Narrative Editing
candidates.evidence: User study with professional and semi-professional writers comparing a graph-based story ideation system with normal AI-based writing workflows; reports better support for creativity and exploration, likely self-reported.

candidates.title: Leveraging LLMs for Design Ideation: An AI Tool to Assist Creativity
candidates.task: small-group design ideation with a speech-based LLM agent
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-assisted ideation sessions using an analogical LLM ideation agent with traditional sessions; preliminary findings rest on participants' own ratings of their ideas.

candidates.title: InkIdeator: Supporting Chinese-Style Visual Design Ideation via AI-Infused Exploration of Chinese Paintings
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing InkIdeator with a baseline system lacking extracted dimensional keywords; reports more effective creative ideation support, largely perceived.

candidates.title: Surprise2Refine: Axis-Centered Exploration-To-Refinement for Agent-Assisted Creative Scaffolding
candidates.task: design exploration and refinement with agents
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study of an axis-centered agent-assisted design tool; it improved sense of control and the perceived creativity of design outcomes relative to the comparison condition.

candidates.title: Brief2Design: A Multi-phased, Compositional Approach to Prompt-based Graphic Design
candidates.task: prompt-based graphic design from client briefs
candidates.evidence: Study with twelve designers comparing a structured multi-phase design tool with conversational baselines; it increased prompt diversity but produced comparable image diversity.

candidates.title: One Tool, One Taste? How Vibe Coding Trades Collective Diversity for Individual Creativity
candidates.task: promotional websites built with a vibe-coding tool
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 73 websites built by graduate students with Lovable for distinct businesses under an originality-graded assignment; image embeddings show strong within-cohort visual concentration (88% of sites in six clusters). No comparison condition.

candidates.title: Writing in Symbiosis: Mapping Human Creative Agency in the AI Era
candidates.task: longitudinal writing before and after LLM deployment
candidates.evidence: Longitudinal corpus analysis of authors' writing before and after LLM deployment finds thematic convergence on AI topics with structured stylistic differentiation rather than uniform homogenization. Context study.

candidates.title: Integrating Flipped Learning and Generative AI for Practice-Based Design Education: Evidence from a Knit Yarn Design Course
candidates.evidence: Exploratory comparison of a historical control cohort (12) with an intervention cohort (16) taught with flipped learning plus a GenAI ideation module; creativity-thinking scores were higher in the intervention cohort, but AI is bundled with other changes.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2026), pp. 198-201
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) finding a small homogenization effect of AI use (d = .334). Likely a short conference version of the collected de Rooij (2026) homogenisation meta-analysis.

candidates.title: The Effects of Human-AI Collaboration on Creativity
candidates.task: word association tasks solo then with an AI agent, AUT before and after
candidates.evidence: Poster: participants did a forward or divergent association task alone and then with an AI agent, with AUT and semantic fluency before and after; collaborative rounds were more original and less variable, and after collaboration AUT fluency rose while originality fell.

candidates.title: Exploring the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Creative Thinking Processes: results from a preliminary study
candidates.venue: Venue not identified (Università Telematica Pegaso IRIS repository record)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with two independent groups, one allowed to use GenAI during the analytical phases before creative production; no significant difference in creative performance.

candidates.title: Effects of Using Generative Artificial Intelligence Collaboration During Idea Generation and Evaluation
candidates.evidence: Undergraduates did an ideation task under different AI engagement conditions, regrouped by behavior (no AI, AI-generated, augmented, prompt engineering); prompt-engineering and augmented use predicted higher idea quality and originality.

candidates.title: GenFODrawing: Supporting Creative Found Object Drawing With Generative AI
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 32
candidates.evidence: Comparative user study of a system offering AI textual and visual inspirations and controllable image generation versus participants' own methods without it; reports easier exploration of diverse ideas and higher creativity support, largely perceived.

candidates.title: Voice Modality, Engagement, and Trust Calibration in Human-AI Co-Creation
candidates.evidence: Research-in-progress pilot comparing voice with text interaction in generative-AI co-creation; voice reduced output quality and widened a trust calibration gap. Whether outputs are creative products is unclear.

candidates.title: Enhancing human computer collaboration in design process: How AI-generated content elevates students’ creativity
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how AI-generated content affects students' creativity in the design process; the abstract could not be retrieved (publisher blocked, Crossref has none), so design is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Augmented Learning for Joint Creativity in Human-AI Co-Creation
candidates.evidence: Title suggests a study of augmented learning for joint human-AI creativity; the abstract could not be retrieved, so design and outcomes are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Creativity: Insights into Idea Generation and Development Using Generative AI
candidates.evidence: Title suggests a study of idea generation and development with generative AI; the abstract could not be retrieved, so design and outcomes are unconfirmed.
